subject: ClearBank request: IR plan, forensic artifacts, and post-incident writeup
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@clearbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@clearbank.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: Incident Response Plan and recent forensics export

Hi Michael,

We're running through our vendor due diligence after a brief auth anomaly last week and need the following from Redwood to close our SIG/SOC2 checklist: a current incident response plan (any version published within the last 12 months), and a forensics export for activity around 2027-04-24 02:00-06:00 UTC (requesting logs and any relevant KV cache snapshots).

Please send the IRP PDF and an evidence bundle or a secure transfer link. We also need a short timeline of actions taken by your ops team during the window. Target for our review is 2027-04-30.

If you prefer, loop in your security operations lead and we can set a 30-min call for clarification.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Head of Third-Party Risk
ClearBank

Attachments: none
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@clearbank.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: Incident Response Plan and recent forensics export

Emma —

Thanks for the note and the clear checklist. We're pulling the artifacts now. I'm attaching our latest IRP (v3) which includes escalation paths, SLOs, and evidence-handling procedures. Diego (forensics) will run the export for the 2027-04-24 window and Naomi (security ops) will provide the incident timeline and any privileged-notification emails.

Quick notes:
- We retain full request/response logs and access logs for 90 days by default; additional retention can be enabled under enterprise contracts.
- The forensics export will include: request logs, node-level access logs, and a sanitized KV-cache snapshot.
- Expect a secure transfer link later today or early tomorrow once Diego completes the packaging and internal review.

If you need anything redacted for privacy before transfer, tell us what fields to remove and we'll sanitize.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Emma / team —

I've completed a scoped export for 2027-04-24 02:00-06:00 UTC. Contents: request-trace-20270424.jsonl (sanitized), node-access-20270424.log, kv-cache-snapshot-20270424.bin, and a short runbook describing how the export was generated. The bundle has been hashed and reviewed by our internal ops team.

I'm preparing the secure transfer link to the Redwood secure-share container. ETA: 2 hours. Per your note about timelines, here's the condensed view of actions taken on 2027-04-24:
- 02:08 UTC: transient auth error detected by automated monitoring (rate spike + 401s)
- 02:10 UTC: automated retry/fallback engaged; no customer-facing impact observed
- 02:14 UTC: ops alert escalated to on-call; key rotation check performed
- 02:35 UTC: suspected upstream auth provider degradation confirmed; routing fallback enabled
- 03:05 UTC: traffic normalized; monitoring cleared at 03:20 UTC

Let me know if you want the full, non-sanitized export under an executed NDA.

- Diego
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: Incident Response Plan and recent forensics export (post-incident writeup attached)

Emma —

Appreciate the quick review. Two quick answers and attached the one-page post-incident writeup you requested.

1) Data redaction: the export was sanitized to remove PII/user content fields. Specifically we removed: payload.body, payload.user_email, and any request headers containing Authorization tokens. Line-level hashes were preserved to allow provenance verification. If you require raw fields for a regulator, we'll need an NDA amendment and a scoped access window.

2) Post-incident summary: attached (postmortem-clearbank-20270429.docx). Summary below:
- Timeline (UTC): 02:08 detection → 03:20 cleared
- Root cause: transient failure in an upstream auth provider causing elevated 401s; our fallback routing did not fully engage for a short window due to a stale cache entry in the routing component.
- Impact: no confirmed customer-visible data exfiltration; <0.1% request latency increase for routed traffic during window.
- Mitigations implemented: invalidation of stale routing caches, added an automated cache-health check to the runbook, and updated rollback play for canary promotions.
- Recommended follow-ups: add an integration test for fallback engagement and extend log retention for the routing component to 180 days for higher-fidelity audits.

Attached also is the sanitized forensic bundle index for your audit pack. If this satisfies the SIG items, please confirm and we'll move to close the ticket on our side.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-clearbank-20270429.docx; forensic-index-20270424.txt
